clinical_note: Duplicate Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) therapy (e.g., Seclo + Sergel/Maxpro). Verify with prescribing doctor to avoid unnecessary dual acid suppression.
Duplicate Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) therapy. Confirm single PPI agent with physician.

Duplicate Paracetamol active ingredient (e.g., Napa + Ace Plus/Napa Extra). Risk of exceeding 4g/day hepatotoxic limit.
Dual Angiotensin Receptor Blocker (ARB) therapy. High risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal injury.
Dual RAAS blockade (ARB + ACE Inhibitor) increases risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and acute kidney injury.
Dual RAAS blockade (ARB + ACE Inhibitor) increases risk of hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury.
Duplicate ARB therapy (Olmesartan inside Bizoran + separate Losartan). Verify regimen with cardiologist.
Duplicate Amlodipine component (Bizoran already contains Amlodipine + Camlodin/Amdocal). Risk of severe hypotension/edema.
Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). Intentional after stent/ACS, but significantly increases GI bleeding risk — verify intended duration.
Concurrent Aspirin + NSAID increases GI ulcer/bleeding risk and may blunt aspirin antiplatelet effect.
High risk of severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage and renal toxicity when combining Ketorolac with Aspirin.
Duplicate NSAID therapy. Additive risk of GI bleed and acute kidney injury.
Duplicate NSAID therapy. Avoid taking two NSAIDs concurrently.
NSAID + ARB can blunt blood pressure control and worsen renal perfusion (especially if also taking a diuretic).
NSAID + Loop Diuretic reduces diuretic efficacy and raises acute kidney injury risk.
Omeprazole/Esomeprazole inhibit CYP2C19 activation of Clopidogrel. Doctors often prefer Pantoprazole (Pantonix) or Rabeprazole (Finix).
Esomeprazole may reduce antiplatelet effect of Clopidogrel via CYP2C19 inhibition. Ask doctor about Pantoprazole.
Duplicate Sulfonylurea therapy. High risk of severe hypoglycemia.
Duplicate Metformin component (e.g., Comet + Galvus Met). Check total daily Metformin dose does not exceed 2000-2550mg.
Duplicate Beta-Blocker therapy. Risk of symptomatic bradycardia and hypotension.
Duplicate Statin therapy. Increases risk of myopathy/elevated liver enzymes without added benefit.
Azithromycin + Domperidone both prolong QT interval. Use caution in cardiac patients.
Additive QT prolongation risk (Moxifloxacin + Domperidone). Avoid concurrent use if cardiac arrhythmia risk exists.
